cards.title: Luki w tekście: co najczęściej wpada
cards.body:
Najczęściej brakuje jednego z tych elementów:
**przyimek** (in advance, out of, depend on), **rodzajnik** (the, a), **zaimek względny** (which, whose, where, who), **czasownik pomocniczy** (have, was, would), **spójnik** (because, although, but), **wyrażenie ilości** (some, many, most), **część czasownika frazowego** (find out, turn off).
Przeczytaj całe zdanie i określ część mowy brakującego słowa, potem wybierz konkretną formę.
cards.tip: W lukach nie wolno używać skróceń (isn't, can't).

cards.title: Past Perfect Continuous i III okres warunkowy
cards.body:
**had been + -ing** – czynność trwała przed innym momentem w przeszłości: She had been waiting for an hour when the bus came.
**III okres warunkowy** – nierealna przeszłość: **If + Past Perfect, would have + III forma**: If he had studied harder, he would have passed.

cards.title: Strona bierna i have something done
cards.body:
Strona bierna we wszystkich czasach: be (w odpowiednim czasie) + III forma: is made, was made, has been made, will be made, is being made, would have been made.
**have/get + dopełnienie + III forma** – usługa wykonana przez kogoś: We are having our car repaired.

cards.title: Mowa zależna z różnymi czasownikami
cards.body:
Po said i told są też czasowniki oddające cel wypowiedzi:
**admit** (to) + -ing: He admitted breaking the window.
**warn** + osoba + (not) to: She warned us not to enter.
**order / advise / remind** + osoba + to: He ordered them to leave.
**suggest** + -ing / that: She suggested going out.

cards.title: Czasowniki modalne w przeszłości
cards.body:
**must have + III forma** – pewny wniosek (She must have forgotten).
**can't / couldn't have + III forma** – pewność, że coś nie zaszło.
**might / may / could have + III forma** – możliwość.
**should have + III forma** – krytyka lub żal (You should have called).
**needn't have + III forma** – zrobione niepotrzebnie.

cards.title: Zwyczaje i przyzwyczajenia
cards.body:
**used to / would** – dawne zwyczaje (would tylko dla czynności).
**be used to + -ing** – być przyzwyczajonym; **get used to + -ing** – przyzwyczajać się.
**had better + bezokolicznik bez to** – lepiej, żebyś: You had better leave now.
**It's high time + Past Simple**: It's high time you went to bed.

cards.title: Imiesłowy, so/such, cleft sentences
cards.body:
**Imiesłów czynny:** Walking home, I met Ben. **Bierny:** Built in 1900, the bridge is still used.
**so + przymiotnik / such + (a/an) + przymiotnik + rzeczownik:** so boring / such a boring film.
**Cleft:** It was Tom who broke the window.
**So am I / Neither am I:** I'm tired. – So am I.

cards.title: Przekształcenia ze słowem kluczowym (rejonowy)
cards.body:
Limit to **pięć wyrazów wliczając podany**; skróconą formę (mustn't) liczymy jako jedno słowo. Podanej formy nie wolno zmienić.
Typowe struktury arkusza: **strona bierna, mowa zależna, have/get something done, wish/if, used to/would, zdania względne z whose, czasowniki frazowe, porównania (so/such, as ... as)**.
Najpierw ustal strukturę, potem sprawdź, czy mieścisz się w limicie.

flash.back: pewność, że coś się nie stało
If + Past Perfect, would have + III forma
zlecić wykonanie usługi: have my hair cut
Past Simple: It's high time you left.

groups.text:
Taking a gap year

Many young people in Europe now decide to take a gap year, which means spending twelve months (1)___ of education or work before starting university. Some travel (2)___ the world, while others volunteer in projects in distant countries, (3)___ they help to build schools or look after animals.

The idea has several advantages. First of all, it gives students time to find (4)___ what they really want to study. A young person who has just left school is often (5)___ sure about the future, and a year of new experiences can change their plans completely. (6)___ addition, living abroad is an excellent way of improving a foreign language, since there is no other choice (7)___ to speak it every day.

Nevertheless, there are also drawbacks. A gap year can be expensive, (8)___ the cost of flights, accommodation and insurance has to be paid by the family. Some parents worry (9)___ their children will lose the habit of studying, and (10)___ of them never return to education at all. Universities, however, usually welcome applicants who (11)___ spent a year doing something useful, because such students tend to be more mature and independent.

If you are thinking of going abroad, plan carefully. It is better to prepare everything well (12)___ advance, to learn at least a few words of the local language and to tell someone at home (13)___ you are at all times. And do not forget that the most important thing is (14)___ the journey itself, but what you learn from it. Anyone (15)___ returns with new skills and a wider view of the world has certainly spent the year well.

Board games, (1)___ many people thought were old-fashioned, have returned in a surprising way. Cafés where customers can play (2)___ a coffee have opened in many cities, and every year publishers present hundreds of new titles (3)___ big fairs.

One reason for this success is that board games offer something that screens (4)___ not: face-to-face contact. Players sit around one table, talk, laugh and sometimes argue, (5)___ the rules of a game are not always clear. In (6)___ of the popularity of video games, many young people say that they prefer an evening with friends and cards to another hour in front of a monitor.

Teachers also (7)___ discovered the educational value of such games. A simple game can teach children (8)___ to count, plan ahead and lose with dignity. Some schools even organise tournaments, (9)___ pupils compete in teams.

Of course, board games are not for everybody. They can take (10)___ time than a quick game on a phone, and a complicated game needs (11)___ least an hour just to learn the rules. Nevertheless, fans insist that the effort is worth (12)___.
